bearings.paper_claim: Dai et al. report that S2V-DQN beats hand heuristics by wide margins on MemeTracker MVC (ratio 1.0021 vs 1.2220 for MVCApprox-Greedy and 1.4080 for MVCApprox) and on Ising MaxCut (1.0223 vs 1.2825 for MaxcutApprox), on one MemeTracker graph and ten Ising instances. The paper does not study budget allocation or separable resource objectives.
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/optimize.py is a lazy greedy (docstring lines 3-11) over per-member chunks of INC, default 500 dollars (line 26), with per-member cap PMAX, default 10000 (line 27). The docstring says the fixed-state objective is separable with diminishing chunk marginals, so the largest marginal is the exact discrete optimum. concavity_violations at line 73 checks this. Replanning after modeled money thresholds does not carry the certificate. The code says lazy greedy; CELF is not named.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's gains are on synthetic graphs and benchmark graph instances, scored against CPLEX best-found values with a one-hour cutoff. The paper says nothing about separable concave allocation, so it gives no support for the optimizer's exactness; that rests only on the code's own docstring and concavity check. A learned replacement would need many training instances, which the system does not have.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers verified in the text. The qualifies relation is analyst inference, not a paper claim. Corrected CELF to lazy greedy: CELF does not appear in optimize.py and the paper does not discuss allocation. Code claims verified: INC default 500, PMAX default 10000, concavity check at line 73.

bearings.paper_claim: On set covering built from the MemeTracker-derived graph, averaged over 1000 test graphs, Dai et al. report ratios of S2V-DQN 1.001, LP 1.0009 and Greedy 1.03. This is minimum set cover, not budgeted maximum coverage, and the paper makes no general claim about coverage objectives.
bearings.paper_location: Appendix C.4 (set covering; text lines 1405-1420), with Appendix B for the SCP setup
bearings.system_side: budgetRecruit in fec/surfaces/templates/make_dashboard_html_00.tpl lines 773-793 scores a candidate by its marginal noisy-OR coverage gain, 1 minus cov[c] plus the sum of PE times (1 minus cov[v]), multiplied by (1 plus 2 dT[c]) when a target is set. Candidates below 0.1 times mean degree are pruned. The loop stops at nSeeds, not at a cost bound. The comment at lines 773-776 calls it cost-bounded, claims the (1-1/e) guarantee, and says no ML is needed at this scale.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Dai's set cover is minimum cover; budgetRecruit is budgeted maximum coverage with a target reweighting and degree pruning, so the 3 percent greedy gap does not transfer directly. 533 nodes is inside Dai's tested range of up to 1200, but there is no training distribution. The guarantee does not hold strictly under the reweighting and pruning.
bearings.verifier_note: Set cover numbers verified (1.001, 1.0009, 1.03 over 1000 test graphs). The generalization to coverage-type objectives is removed: the paper reports only set cover. Code claims verified: loop bounded by nSeeds, 1 plus 2dT factor, 0.1 mean-degree pruning, and the comment overclaims the guarantee. The comment attributes its grounding to GCOMB (Manchanda), not Dai.

bearings.paper_claim: A Q-function over a graph embedding, trained by n-step Q-learning with fitted Q-iteration, can serve as a greedy evaluation function and generalizes from 50-100 node training graphs to 1000-1200 node test graphs, with MaxCut BA ratio 1.0038 and MVC BA ratio 1.0062 (Table 2, 1000 test instances).
bearings.system_side: build_route in fec/engine/cosponsor_route.py lines 41-56 is a greedy over candidate edges, with a heap keyed by (gain minus lam times (1 minus p)) divided by edge cost CEDGE over max(0.1, p). K defaults to 5 recruits per recruiter (line 9), and the loop stops when the best value is at most zero. The non-submodular sibling closedCascadeRoute in the template at lines 824-835 is explicitly labeled a sequential heuristic with no (1-1/e) claim.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Requires a simulated instance distribution, for example cascades on perturbed or topic-specific kernels, as training data, which the system lacks. A learned Q-value is a heuristic score, never an ask-success or access probability (D-025). Any result stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper side verified in Table 2 and Section 5.2. System side verified: K default and the edge score. Wording corrected: the risk penalty sits inside the numerator before division by edge cost, not as value per dollar minus lambda times risk. The closedCascadeRoute comment is verified.

Verified: RL4CCIM says it builds on the Khalil 2017 and RL4IM line (text lines 395-413) and uses a graph attention network encoder (line 484).

Partly verified: Kamarthi says previous graph RL work [13], which is Khalil et al. 2017 in its reference list, did not use a distinct global representation (text around line 215). The closest prior work phrasing is not in the text. Internal item slug is kamarthi-2019 (arXiv 1907.11625) while the filename says 2020.

RELINK (CIKM 2025) does not cite Dai 2017, S2V, GCOMB or Khalil 2017; its only Khalil reference is the 2014 KDD paper. It is a parallel closed-network RL line, not a descendant. The RELINK design attribution in the closedCascadeRoute code comment is verified.
Dai's n-step Q-learning cites Sutton and Barto 1998 [36], not Watkins; fitted Q-iteration cites Riedmiller [33]. The Watkins link is conceptual, not a citation.
Dai does not cite Golovin. The link runs through Melange: the optimize.py docstring keeps a Golovin-Krause upper bound as a diagnostic (verified). Conceptual, not from the paper.
Dai cites the classical Kempe et al. influence maximization paper as reference [20] (text line 796). The item year 2015 may differ from the 2003 KDD original; link kept as a conceptual complement.

summary_issues: Summary says the joint optimizer is a CELF lazy greedy. optimize.py says lazy greedy only; CELF does not appear in the file.
Summary says the paper's evidence suggests a learned score adds little where greedy is near-optimal. Dai et al. make no such claim; it is analyst inference from a 3 percent set cover gap.
Summary says RELINK belongs to the learned-greedy line that Dai starts. RELINK's text does not cite Dai, S2V or GCOMB, so it is a parallel line, not a descendant.
Summary gives GCOMB's benchmark as S2V-DQN 0.87 vs greedy 0.89 at b=15. The values appear in GCOMB's BP-2k row; the b=15 setting was not verified.
Summary says Melange has one 533-member graph per Congress. Not verified in this pass; the repo and vault were not checked for per-Congress structure.
Summary implies the set cover gap generalizes to coverage-type objectives. The paper reports only minimum set cover on one MemeTracker-derived graph.
